newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO restores Bosnia's east-west railway.
newsitem.headline: NATO restores Bosnia's east-west railway.

text.p: The NATO-led peace force said on Monday engineers have repaired an east-west railway linking Bosnia to the rest of Europe.
The work restored a vital rail connection for the first time since fighting ended a year ago.

The repair of a bridge at Bosansko Petrovo Selo in northern Bosnia completed a reconstruction effort connecting Bosnia's railway to neighbouring Croatia in the west and Serbia in the east, said a spokesman for the NATO-led peace Implementation Force (IFOR).
"It is now possible to travel by rail from Zagreb into and through Bosnia-Herzegovina to Belgrade," Major Brett Boudreau told reporters.
The bridge at Bosansko Petrovo Selo was damaged during 43 months of fighting as it lies between Serb-held Doboj and Bosnian government territory.

The 300 km (186 miles) rail link, crossing former front lines twice, will allow NATO to move its 58,000-strong force and equipment more easily as well as lay the foundation for the country's peacetime reconstruction, Boudreau said.
Despite progress in repairing work, NATO officers say rival Bosnian authorities have been slow to react and appeared reluctant to quickly reopen the railway.
As of September, railway companies had no immediate plans to start running regular commercial or passenger trains on the route.
"Unfortunately politics is still an obstacle, not the engineering," said one officer.
Bosnia's two major railway tracks, one running north-south and the other east-west, form a T-shaped net which was severely damaged during the war.
Fragments of the network functioned for military purposes of Bosnia's warring factions, but trains never crossed front lines, where tracks and bridges were destroyed as a rule.
The track between Sarajevo and the Adriatic port of Ploce in Croatia was repaired in July. But the other portion of north-south line between Sarajevo and Doboj in the north has yet to be repaired.
